Package frc.robot.subsystems.turret

Interface TurretIO

All Known Implementing Classes:
TurretIODisabled, TurretIOHardware, TurretIOSim
public interface TurretIO
Hardware abstraction interface for the turret mechanism.

IO Layer Pattern

Rather than calling TalonFX or CANcoder directly, Turret calls this interface. Three implementations are selected at startup:
  • TurretIOHardware â€” talks to real CTRE hardware over CAN.
  • TurretIOSim â€” drives simulated motor physics; matches hardware behavior well enough to test control loops in simulation without a robot.
  • TurretIODisabled â€” all calls are no-ops; safe for replay and unit tests.
The pattern keeps all hardware-specific code in one place, making the subsystem itself testable in isolation and safe to run during development.

Contract

  • Implementations must update inputs in-place inside updateInputs(frc.robot.subsystems.turret.TurretIO.TurretIOInputs); callers store the inputs object and read from it for the rest of the loop.
  • setPosition(edu.wpi.first.units.measure.Angle) commands the mechanism toward a target angle using MotionMagic (on hardware). It is the only output method â€” there is no voltage or percent-output mode.
  • calibrate() must be called when the turret is known to be at the home/limit-switch position. It zeros the CANcoder so subsequent position reads are field-valid.

  • Method Details

    • updateInputs

      void updateInputs(TurretIO.TurretIOInputs inputs)
      Reads the latest sensor values from hardware and writes them into inputs. Called once per loop cycle by Turret.periodic().
      Parameters:
      inputs - mutable object to update in-place; the same instance is reused every loop

    • setPosition

      void setPosition(edu.wpi.first.units.measure.Angle position)
      Commands the turret toward the given mechanism angle using MotionMagic. The implementation may call this as often as every loop cycle; MotionMagic handles smooth acceleration and deceleration internally.
      Parameters:
      position - target mechanism angle (in any Angle unit â€” implementations convert to rotations internally)

    • calibrate

      void calibrate()
      Zeros the encoder at the current physical position, declaring it the home reference. Called once at startup when the turret is confirmed to be at the limit switch. After this call, TurretIO.TurretIOInputs.calibrated should return true.
